page: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, it features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz using the Neoverse-N1 model. The CPU configuration allocates 1 thread per core, providing a total of 4 vCPUs. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1489.98, placing it in the average tier, whereas the multi-core score of 5934.04 is categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block uncached reads at 71.14 GB/sec and writes at 34.79 GB/sec, but cached small-block reads are weak at 236.0 GB/sec. Geekbench metrics, including software compiling and ray tracing, fall into the weak category. Cryptographic performance is poor, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 538.3, despite hardware AES support.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6g.xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads without the premium of x86 licensing. However, users must navigate tradeoffs, such as the lack of local NVMe storage and the absence of advanced vector or matrix extensions like AVX and AMX. Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and moderate single-core throughput, this instance is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, Redis caching, and lightweight database operations that do not require high-performance multi-core scaling or intensive cryptographic processing.
